name: Process Explainer 3D
description: Master 3D template for any explainer, tutorial, story or comparison: how something works, how it is built, how to do it, what happened, why it happens, A versus B. ONE continuous low-poly world (a persistent `stage`) in soft daylight with a warm key light, built from parametric builders (laptop, router, server-rack, house, castle, ship, planet, cell, factory, bridge, desk, chart-3d, person with costumes and 40 more) that changes over time through word-timed beats while the camera establishes, dives in, follows and pulls out. Diegetic overlay kit (flow, concept, limit, versus), automatic non-overlapping callout labels, and small word-by-word captions (white with a dark outline) near the middle of the frame. Five documented recipes in this one template: build-process, how-it-works, what-happened, cause-effect, compare. Use it instead of engineering-explainer for any stage-based video. No emoji.
prompt_hint: 5-9 scenes (4-8 s) about ONE topic of any kind: a tutorial, a mechanism, a history, a science idea, a product comparison, a process. Build the world ONCE in a top-level `stage` (concept, world scenery, actors, optionally terrain with strata and liquids) from `{ "build": "<name>", "params": {...}, "seed": n }` calls (run `node cli.mjs builders` for the catalog with params): pick builders that fit the subject (tech: laptop, router, data-cable, server-rack, chip; nature: planet, atom, cell, plant, mountain, volcano; history: castle, ship, map-table, cart, tent, person costumes; city: building, bridge, road, factory, crane, wind-turbine; office: desk, chart-3d, coin-stack, safe, calendar). NEVER a new world per scene and never loop presets: every state change is a beat in a scene's `beats` timed to a narration word, and the camera moves with `shots` (wide, zoom-to a focus, dive, low, orbit-like pulls). Pick one recipe: build-process, how-it-works, what-happened, cause-effect or compare (see the 3D section of the spec-writer prompt). Overlays: concept pill, flow, limit, versus. Titles stay short; captions word by word near the middle (small, white with a dark outline). No emoji.
best_for: tutorials and how-to explainers (software, hardware, networks, cooking, DIY)
how a mechanism or system works (machines, energy, finance, the body)
stories and history told as a timeline with characters
science and nature: why something happens
comparisons: A versus B, before and after

build-process.subject: An assembly or construction process, for example building a wind farm or a wooden cart.
build-process.when: Something is made step by step: construction, assembly, installation, cooking, a recipe.
build-process.beats: show the empty site -> prepare the ground (terrain carve or raise) -> bring in the parts (actor pos from above, visible) -> assemble in order (each part appears on a word) -> finish and test (the rotor turns, the load lifts) -> pull out to the result.
build-process.shots: wide -> zoom-to the site -> zoom-to each step -> pullout.
build-process.builders: crane, wind-turbine, factory, cart, slab, rebar-grid, house, person (hard-hat), road

how-it-works.subject: A technology flow, for example a web request from a browser to a server and back.
how-it-works.when: A system moves something through stages: data, power, money, water.
how-it-works.beats: show the whole chain -> a signal (data-cable dot or a glowing part) travels stage by stage, one beat per hop -> highlight each stage as it is reached (emissive, scale pop) -> the result appears -> pull out. Pair it with a `flow` overlay whose active chip follows the hops.
how-it-works.shots: wide -> zoom-to each stage in order -> wide.
how-it-works.builders: laptop, phone, router, data-cable, server-rack, database-cylinder, chip, building, cloud

what-happened.subject: A historical event with characters, for example the voyage of a kingdom's first ship.
what-happened.when: An event or story told in 4-7 moments with people and places.
what-happened.beats: the world before -> a council or trigger (characters gesture, a token moves on the map) -> the journey (an actor travels along the stage) -> the turning point -> the outcome (a flag is raised) -> the consequence.
what-happened.shots: wide -> zoom-to the characters -> follow the traveller -> pullout over the result.
what-happened.builders: castle, map-table, ship, cart, tent, flag, person (crown, helmet, pirate), mountain, road

cause-effect.subject: A physics or biology idea, for example why a volcano erupts or how a cell makes energy.
cause-effect.when: One force or process produces a visible effect: heat, pressure, growth, orbit.
cause-effect.beats: the stable state -> the hidden cause appears (a liquid level, a glowing part, a limit overlay) -> the threshold is crossed (the overlay turns red) -> the effect (lift, eruption, growth) -> the fix or the loop closes.
cause-effect.shots: wide -> zoom-to the cause -> dive in -> pullout to the effect.
cause-effect.builders: volcano, planet, atom, cell, plant, mountain, river, pipe-run, valve, pool

compare.subject: A product A versus B, for example two energy systems or two phones.
compare.when: Two options on one stage: methods, designs, before and after.
compare.beats: place A and B side by side in the same world -> run the same trigger on both (the same beat on each actor) -> show the different outcomes (charge, speed, cost bar) -> versus overlay with the verdict.
compare.shots: wide -> zoom-to A -> zoom-to B -> wide with a versus overlay.
compare.builders: solar-panel, wind-turbine, battery, phone, laptop, car-lowpoly, desk, chart-3d, coin-stack, safe
